0.00229: Housekeeping: a tool for the owner reads the play stats straight from the collector (tools/reports.mjs); nothing changes in the game.
0.00228: Benchmark round: 0.00228 — 0.00227's note named 0.00226, another build that landed first; a benchmark from 0.00227 does not count, please run it once more on this build.
0.00227: Card light: every card now draws its glow on a canvas of its own, handed from room to room, instead of copying each card's picture out of one hidden canvas every frame (the iPhone spent 13 ms a tick on that at rest).
A new benchmark round (0.00226): please run the benchmark again on each device — the Great Hall asks once past room 6, the ?debug BENCHMARK button any time.
0.00226: A new typeface: D-DIN Condensed Bold, free to use (Open Font License), replaces the old DIN Condensed — the look is the same, the font is a third of the download
0.00225: Device reports: every run and benchmark now sends a small performance report with the play stats (frame-time histogram, time per subsystem, stalls with what was happening, the renderer's settings) — anonymous, never stored in your save.
Play stats: a Device reports card with Copy / Copy all; the benchmark round is 0.00225, so the Great Hall asks once more.
0.00224: Play stats: the By build table shows the newest ten builds and the three most played older ones; the save-code entry is gone — every tester is collected.
0.00223: A death in a Sealed Reliquary now counts the room it led to, in your records and on the end screen.
A potion drunk between rooms no longer leaves phantom armor for the next fight; summons are never marked elite.
Benchmark: the Great Hall's ask waits for the hall to settle and its Continue always starts it; the ?debug button returns where it was pressed.

Music and narrator: MUSIC OFF or NARRATOR OFF no longer downloads the score or the takes; NARRATOR OFF stops the line playing; the welcome line no longer waits behind the music; a bed asked for while the music was switched off and on is the one that plays.
Narrator: a line dropped for waiting too long can still play later; with SOUND OFF no line is spent; a short sound under a narrator line no longer cuts the music's return short.
Phones: the save dialogs sit at the top for the keyboard; long room titles stay clear of XP and COINS; the boons sit beside the menu in shrine and treasure rooms; Push Deeper fits on every phone.
A narrow desktop window scrolls the Great Hall to Descend; the treasure room fits a MacBook-height window without a scrollbar.

Smoother: the glowing text (rare items, low health, the death and victory titles) no longer repaints every frame; the battle line writes only what changed; OVERKILL's banner is placed from the cards still standing.
If a screen fails to open, a Reload button appears instead of a blank window; a dialog opened mid-fade hears the keyboard; the display font is a third of its size.
Play stats: a bad run record no longer blanks the dashboard, and the collector agrees with the page on every field (Worker 0.00223 to paste).
0.00222: Phones: a lighter picture — the background at a lower resolution and rest rate, a thinner mist buffer, 1x particles, the card glow at 20 fps, the figures without their drop shadow (the same look, fewer pixels; the owner's iPhone ran hot)
BATTERY SAVER in the corner column: the smallest background and no mist, for a hot phone or a long session; remembered per browser
The room change no longer stalls the game for a quarter second: the painting is decoded off the main thread, and the heavy work is split over two frames
The vignette is drawn by the background's shaders, the glint by transforms, the glow loops as breathing layers, the particle layer is hidden between bursts: less work for every screen every frame

Play stats: the refresh rate is read from the busiest frame interval (120 Hz Macs read 144, iPhones 90 or 75 before, with every ordinary frame 'dropped'); stalls and the worst frame's moment are recorded; old rows are graded by their fps
The benchmark measures each room at rest — a new round, so everyone is asked again; about 50 seconds now

The benchmark round moved with it: a benchmark from an older build is asked again
0.00219: The benchmark ask is back for everyone: once your best room reaches 6, the Great Hall asks once for a 40-second scripted fight (a new round, so a benchmark from an older build is asked again)

Numbers that change glow and grow for a moment — XP and coins in combat, and the row you just bought in the Great Hall (Precision LV2 flashes to LV3, 3/4 potions to 4/4)
